subject.title: feat(chat): UX-012 — token usage progress meter

question: Should this new web chat token meter hide stale `totalTokens` like the current web/Android context indicators, or intentionally show a clearly labeled stale/updating state?
rationale: Both choices are plausible UI policy, but mixing a raw live-looking meter with existing freshness-aware context displays would create conflicting session-state semantics.

options.title: Reuse the freshness-aware model
options.body: Hide the meter or render an unknown state when `totalTokensFresh` is false, matching current web and Android context indicators.

options.title: Show stale usage explicitly
options.body: Render stale totals only with visible stale/updating semantics and tests shared with the context notice policy.

options.title: Pause for stale-display alignment
options.body: Wait until the stale-context indicator PR settles the shared stale-token display convention before landing this UX addition.

recommendation.title: Reuse the freshness-aware model
recommendation.body: Hide the meter or render an unknown state when `totalTokensFresh` is false, matching current web and Android context indicators.

likelyOwner.reason: BunsDev owns this PR and has prior Control UI context/usage history, making them the best available owner for the UX policy choice.
